text.S1: There once was a little girl whose hair was bright and yellow ,and it glittered in the sun like spun-gold. Her name was Goldi-Locs.

text.T2: Kuciindi cimwi kwakali kana kasimbi kakajisi masusu aamwekw mwekw alimwi kuti zuba lyabala akali kumweka mbuli ngolide. Izina lyakwe lyakali Goldi-Locs.

text.S1: One day Goldi-Locs went out to gather flowers. She wandered on and on, and after a while she came to a forest, where she had never been before. She went into the forest, which was very cool and shady.
text.T1: Bumwi buzuba Goldi-Locs wakaya kukubwezelela maluba.Wakazinguluka ooku akooku ,nikwakainda kaindi wakasika mucoonde ncaakatana abuzuba wasika. Wakaya mucoonde cakali aacimvule citontola.
text.T2: Bumwi buzuba Goldi-Locs wakaya kukubwezelela maluba. Wakazinguluka ooku akooku, nokwakainda kaindi wakasika mucoonde ncaatakana abuzuba wasika. Wakaya mucoonde cakali aacimvule citontola.

text.S1: She came to a house standing all alone in the forest. She knocked at the door, as she was tired, hungry and thirsty, and she hoped the good people inside would give her some food and drink, and let her rest a little while.
text.T1: Wakasika a kaanda kakaimvwi akalikke mucoonde. Wakakonkomona kumulyango,mbwaakakatede,anzala alimwi anyota, wakalaalushomo kuti bantu bakali munga`anda oomu inga kabaya kumupa cakulya, cakunywa akumuleka kuti alyookezye kwakaindi kasyoonto.
text.T2: wakasika akaanda kakaimvwi kalikke mucoonde. Wakakonkkomona kumulyango, nkaambo wakalikatedealimwi wakali aanyota, wakali aalushomo kuti bantu babotu bakali mukati inga kabaya kumupa cakulya acakunya, akumuleka kuti alyookezye kwkaindi kasyoonto.

text.S1: Although Goldi-Locs did not know it, this house belonged to three lions. There was GREAT BIG FATHER LION, mid-sized mother lion, and dear little baby lion who was no bigger than Goldi-Locs. The three lions had gone out for a walk while their supper was cooling, so when Goldi-Locs knocked at the door no one answered.
text.T1: Ncaatakazi Goldi-Locs ncakuti kaanda aaka kakali kaanda kabasyuumbwa botatwe. Kwakali syuumbwa mupati wisi, waakati-kati banyina, akasyuumbwa kana ikakali musela wa Goldi -Locs. Aaba basyuumbwa botatwe bakainkide kukweendeenda ciindi cakulya cabo camangolezya nicakacili kutontola, aboobo Goldi-Loc.s naakakonkomona kwiina wakavuwa
text.T2: Ncaatakazi Goldi-Locs ncakuti, aaka kakali kaanda kabasyuumbwa botatwe. Kwakali syuumbwa mupati wisi, waakati-kati banyina, akasyuumbwa kana ikakali musela wa Goldi-Locs. text.S1: She paused and she knocked again. As nobody answered she pushed the door open and stepped inside. There in a row stood three chairs. One was a GREAT BIG CHAIR, and it belonged to the father lion. And one was a middling-sized chair, and it belonged to the mother lion, and one was a dear little chair, and it belonged to the baby lion. And on the table stood three bowls of smoking hot porridge. “And so,” thought Goldi-Locs, “people must be coming back soon to eat it.”
text.T1: Wakaleka kwakaindi kasyoonto mpoona wakonkomona alimwi. Naakabona kuti kwiina wakavwiila wakacitonta citendele akunjila mukati. Wakabona zyuuno zyotatwe zyakayalidwe mumulongo. Cuuno cakutaanguna cakali cipati kapati, eeci cakali cuuno ca syuumbwa wisi. Mpoona kwakali cuuno caakati-kati, eeci cakali cuuno ca syuumbwa banyina, kumamanino kwakali kauno kasyoonto kabotu, aaka kakali kauno kakasyuumbwa kana. text.S1: She thought she would sit down and rest until they came. First she sat down in the GREAT BIG CHAIR, but the cushion was too soft. It seemed as though it would swallow her up. Then she sat down in the middle-sized chair, and the cushion was too hard, and it was not comfortable. Then she sat down in the dear little chair, and it was just right. It fitted her as though it had been made for her. So there she sat, and she rocked and she rocked, and she sat and she sat, until with her rocking and her sitting she sat the bottom right out of it.
text.T1: Wakayeeya kuti inga wakkala alyookezye kusikila balaamunzi bapiluke. Wakakkala aacuuno cipati kapati, pele cuuno eeci cakali citeteete kapati. Cakalikulibonya mbuli kuti inga kaciya kumumena. Mpoona wakakkala aacuuno caakati-kati, eeci cakali ciyumu kapati aboobo kwiina naakalikwaya pe. Mpoona wakakkala aakauno kasyoonto kabotu, aaka kauno kakamukkwana mbuli kuti kakapangilidwe nguwe. Aboobo wakakkala akulicenka, mwaakali kucucauka akulicenka wakakapandula kauno kulubazu lwaansi lwalulyo.

text.S1: And nobody had come, and there stood three bowls of porridge on the table. “They must not be very hungry people,” thought Goldi-Locs to herself. Or they would have come home to eat their supper.” And she went over to the table just to see whether the bowls were full.

The second bowl was a middle-sized bowl, with a middle-sized wooden spoon in it, and that was the mother lion’s bowl. And the third bowl was a dear little bowl, with a dear little silver spoon in it, and that was the baby lion’s bowl.

text.S1: The porridge that was in the bowls smelled so very good that Goldi-Locs thought she would taste it.

text.T2: Ceele cakali mumitiba eeyi cakali kununkillila kapati cakuti Goldi-Locs wakayeeya kuti acilabile.

text.S1: She took the GREAT BIG SPOON and tasted the porridge in the GREAT BIG BOWL, but it was too hot. Then she took the middle-sized spoon and tasted the porridge in the middle-sized bowl, and it was too cold. Then she took the little silver spoon and tasted the porridge in the dear little bowl, and it was just right. It tasted so good that she tasted and tasted, and tasted and tasted until she tasted it all up.
text.T1: Wakabweza conco mupati kapati akulabila ceele cakali mumutiba mupati kapati, pesi ceele eeci cakali kupya kapati. The second bed was a middling-sized bed that belonged to the mother lion, and the third bed was a dear little bed that belonged to the dear little baby lion.

text.S1: Goldi-Locs lay down on the GREAT BIG BED to try it, but the pillow was too firm and she wasn’t comfortable at all.

text.S1: While Goldi-Locs was still asleep in the little bed, the three lions came home again, and as soon as they stepped inside the door and looked around, they knew that somebody had been there.
